test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the impact of proportional taxes?

options.text: Increases the marginal propensity to consume

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduces the autonomous expenditure multiplier**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proportional taxes** are taxes that maintain a consistent rate regardless of income level.
 
• These taxes **reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier** because they decrease disposable income, leading to lower consumption and investment.
 
• The **autonomous expenditure multiplier** is a measure of the change in aggregate output caused by a change in autonomous spending.
 
• When disposable income is reduced, the overall consumption in the economy decreases, thereby reducing the multiplier effect.
 
• In contrast, the **induced expenditure multiplier** is influenced by changes in income levels and marginal propensities to consume.
 
• Proportional taxes do not increase the induced expenditure multiplier; rather, they generally have a contractionary effect on the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **marginal propensity to consume (MPC)** is the fraction of additional income that a household consumes rather than saves.
 
• Proportional taxes do not directly affect the MPC but can influence overall consumption patterns by reducing disposable income.
 
• Understanding the impact of different types of taxes on multipliers is crucial for designing effective fiscal policies.
 
• Fiscal policy tools, such as altering tax rates and government spending, are used to manage economic activity and achieve macroeconomic objectives.
 
• Effective fiscal policy can help stabilize the economy, promote growth, and reduce unemployment.
